variants.name: Current architecture
variants.summary: Service level: browser as implemented on 2026-09-13. Follow linked subjects for related levels.

nodes.name: Archboard system
nodes.description: Context above this service: the canvas server, CLI, board files, browser, and Codex workbench together form Archboard.

nodes.name: Browser client
nodes.description: The desktop-only read client. It owns presentation state and sends commands, while board meaning and drawing remain server-owned.

nodes.name: Application composition
nodes.description: Composes shell, pane sessions, semantic viewer, workbench, routing, notices, settings, and voice around shared browser state.

nodes.name: Semantic viewer
nodes.description: Fetches server-rendered semantic boards and owns only camera, selection, view, variant, walkthrough, and drill-down presentation.

nodes.name: Pane session
nodes.responsibility: Keeps each pane in server contact
nodes.description: Owns pane registration, socket generations, current semantic reading reports, and the workbench transport carried by the pane socket.

nodes.name: Workspace routing
nodes.description: Maps pane board keys and active pane to URL state, preflights navigation, and applies browser history without becoming board authority.

nodes.name: Board catalog
nodes.description: Owns the cached server listing and provider used by navigation surfaces to find persisted semantic boards.

nodes.name: Workbench client
nodes.description: Renders the focused pane's Codex session from server snapshots and deltas and sends user actions through the pane transport.

nodes.name: Voice session
nodes.description: Coordinates realtime voice, narration, approval speech, media level, and semantic context supplied by the active pane.

nodes.name: Code target
nodes.description: Turns a selected semantic node's persisted repo and path binding into an opener request through the host shell.

nodes.name: Canvas server
nodes.responsibility: Serves pictures and live session state
nodes.description: Authoritative server peer reached through HTTP reads, pane WebSockets, workbench messages, and code-opening requests.

walkthroughs.name: Reading a board in the browser

beats.heading: Restore the workspace
beats.body: Routing supplies opaque board keys; application composition asks pane sessions to open them and keeps the active pane visible.

beats.heading: Read the server's drawing
beats.body: The semantic viewer fetches the board document and rendered SVG, then owns camera, selection, views, variants, walkthroughs, and local drill-down only.

beats.heading: Carry the active context
beats.body: The pane socket reports what is actually on screen and carries the bound workbench; voice and code opening act through their narrow browser owners.
